Hi, Greg,
Sorry for that I forgot to send my R code, which is as follows:
forestplot.gg <- function(s){
# s is a data frame with 4 columns
# s$x gives variable names
# s$y gives center point
# s$yl gives lower limits
# s$yu gives upper limits
require(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(d, aes(x=x, y=y, ymin=yl, ymax=yu))+
scale_color_manual(values = "darkblue")
+geom_pointrange(colour="darkblue",size=1, shape=15)+
coord_flip(xlim = NULL) +
geom_hline(aes(x=0),colour="darkblue", lty=3)+ xlab('Genes')+
ylab('Blood CL')+scale_y_continuous(limits=c(20, 67))+
opts(panel.background = theme_rect(fill='white',
colour='red'),
axis.title.x = theme_text(family = "sans", size = 10,face =
"bold",hjust = 0.7, vjust = 1),
axis.title.y = theme_text(family = "sans", size = 10,face =
"bold",hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1, angle = 90),
axis.text.x = theme_text(hjust=1, size=9,face="bold"),
axis.text.y = theme_text(hjust=1, size=9,face="bold"))+
opts(title = "Blood &
Genes",plot.title=theme_text(size=12,family = "sans",face =
"bold",hjust = 0.6,vjust = 1))+
opts(plot.margin = unit(c(1.4, 1,1.5,0), "lines"))
return(p)
}
forestplot.gg(s)

If my data s has more than 24 observations, my forest plot shows wrong
dots. Would you please giving me some clues?
Thanks a lot!
